posts.caption:
✨ Big news from Drag Church! ✨

In 2024, Drag Church began as an experiment.
Something beautiful happened.

Today, we’re excited to share the next chapter. Drag Church is becoming part of something even bigger.

Introducing Kinship Collaborative! A new community-centered organization that will serve as the umbrella for Drag Church, Drag Story Time, Drag Summer Camp, Queer Youth Homelessness Prevention Initiatives, a Gender Affirming Clothing Closet, and future programs designed to help LGBTQIA2S+ youth and allies connect, create, heal, learn, and belong.

❤️ Drag Church isn’t going anywhere.
It remains one of Kinship Collaborative’s signature programs and will continue to be the joyful, spiritually inclusive gathering that started it all.

This evolution allows us to dream bigger, build deeper partnerships, pursue fiscal sponsorship, foster more opportunities for community care, and create a future where everyone has a place to belong.

This is only the beginning.

Thank you for believing in this work, volunteering, performing, donating, partnering with us, and showing up with your whole heart. You’re helping build this.

The movement is growing. Because belonging was never meant to be limited.
🌈💜

#KinshipCollaborative #SeattleArts #pride🌈 #grassrootsseattle QueerSeattle

posts.caption:
When Kitty Smith @kitty.zero.hour @yassifyjesus, an artist disgruntled with Trump’s reelection, began to draw dragified versions of Jesus in 2024 to protest the increasing negativity toward LGBTQIA+ people across the country, never did she expect her idea to “yassify Jesus” would transform into a full-blown, flamboyant church service. 

Working with Kara Sutra @kara.sutra (the drag mother of the @hausofsutra), she had decided a year ago to create a nonreligious, all-ages space for LGBTQIA+ people to build community together, called Drag Church. Now as they move toward their first anniversary, the duo plan to up the ante of extravagance and community engagement with the upcoming service, aptly named “REBIRTH.” 

Read the full article online at www.sgn.org, or in our April 2026 issue out now!

Photo credit: Jesse Sieden

posts.caption:
I’m still finding words for what this night meant. To everyone who has supported Drag Church along the way, and to every single person who came out for The Yassification of Ebenezer Scrooge, thank you, from the deepest place in my heart.

The outpouring of joy filled this space in ways I will never forget. What we experienced together was proof that when we gather with open hearts, something sacred happens.

Drag Church reminds us that choosing yourself changes everything. That when one person lights their candle, it quietly tells others, it’s safe here. And even if you’re not in a place where it’s safe to fully be yourself yet, this community sees you. We hold you. We are here for you always. Your light matters. 

To our incredible cast and crew and every person who believed in this vision, you make this magic possible. Thank you for helping us build this community that honors the sacredness of every human spirit because everyone deserves to feel holy in their own bodies. This was one night, but the candles we lit together will continue to glow.

Production @yassifyjesus & @hausofsutra 
Performers @bjblessings @thebrandi_marx @kara.sutra @sid_seedy @jizzuhbelljohnson

There is something so beautiful about watching young people be given the space to fully be themselves and embraced in the ever-expanding possibilities of what it means to be human. 🌈✨

Every child deserves the opportunity to explore their creativity, imagination, joy, and unique potential without shame or limitation. We are so grateful to be part of creating the kinds of spaces we wish existed growing up, and we can’t wait to see where this path leads. 

Thank you @bridgeschoolcooperative for hosting us and to @whitecenterpride for sponsorship the event!

Also big shout out to our photographer and videographer @jesse_sieden for capturing the magic!

posts.caption:
Today was a celebration of imagination and loving ourselves exactly as we are 🌈✨

We had such a beautiful time bringing Drag Story Time to @bridgeschoolcooperative alongside the incredible sponsorship of @whitecenterpride ! Together, we read stories, learned about the colors of the Pride flag, asked questions, danced, created art, and celebrated the magic that happens when young people are encouraged to show up fully as themselves. 

Watching these kiddos decorate their own flags, share their curiosity, and light up with confidence reminded us why this work matters so deeply. Inclusive literacy and creative spaces help build a future where every child knows they belong.

A huge thank you to The Bridge School for welcoming us so warmly into your community and to White Center Price for sponsoring the event. 💫

And this is just the beginning…

Drag Story Time is expanding into programming for ALL ages from schools and youth spaces to community organizations, workshops, creative gatherings, and intergenerational events.

If you’d like to bring Drag Story Time or inclusive arts programming to your organization, send us a DM! Tell us your goals, your community, and your vision and let’s create something beautiful together 🌈✨

#seattledrag #inclusiveliteracy #dragchurch #dragstorytime #seattle
